item.research_question: How does high-strain deformation influence the transition between chemical clustering and ordering in an Al0.1CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy, and what are the underlying mechanisms compared to tensile loading?
item.material_system: Al0.1CrCoFeNi (quinary high-entropy alloy with Al mole fraction x = 0.1)
item.processing_route: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using a derived EAM-LJ force-field; alloy melted at 2,200 K, quenched at 21.11 K/ps to 300 K, then deformed at a strain rate of 10^10 s^-1 under NPT/NVT/NVE ensembles
item.test_conditions: Compressive and tensile loading at temperatures of 77 K, 300 K, 700 K, and 1,000 K; strain rates of 10^10 s^-1; engineering strain up to 0.9%
key_findings: A peak flow stress of ~125 MPa is recorded for compressive loading at 77 and 300 K, dropping to ~90 MPa at 700 and 1,000 K.
Under compressive loading, a clustering-to-ordering transition occurs with an increase in unlike pair correlations (e.g., Al-Co, Al-Cr) and a decrease in like pair correlations (e.g., Al-Al).
No strain hardening is observed under tensile deformation, whereas compressive loading shows marked evidence of strain hardening.
The Al-Ni pair possesses the strongest interchange-energy fluctuations at a long-wavelength (k = [000]), driving clustering behavior.
The calculated spinodal temperature (Tsp) is 840 K, which agrees with the experimentally-observed transition temperature of 813–823 K.
Large fluctuations in stress under compressive loading at elevated temperatures are attributed to thermo-plastic instability in the shear band.
The lattice parameter (a0) predicted by MD simulations is 3.55 Å at 0 K, in reasonable agreement with KKR-CPA (3.51–3.57 Å) and experiment (3.57 Å).
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the clustering-to-ordering transition under compression to atomistic rearrangements at high strains, where the high-strain compression promotes the formation of unlike pairs. Conversely, tensile loading induces a plastic flow condition similar to wire-drawing, maintaining the clustering phase. The large fluctuations at high temperatures are caused by thermo-plastic instability leading to shear-induced disordering.
item.limitations: The study notes that the high strain rates (~10^10 s^-1) chosen are due to length and time scale limitations in MD simulations and restrict the use of experimentally-realizable high strain rates (~10^2 s^-1). Additionally, the 'size effect' including local site displacements is not included in the linear-response (k;T) calculations.
item.future_work: The investigation provides further motivation for the experimental exploration of high-temperature compressive thermo-plastic instability in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
quotes: high-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, resulting in a clustering-to-ordering transition that is absent for tensile loading.
The diverging Al-Ni pair of ααβ (k = [000]) at the spinodal temperature (Tsp) indicates the absolute instability of the alloy that forces clustering in Al0.1CrCoFeNi
This thermo-plastic instability in Al0.1CrCoFeNi leads to shear-induced disordering similar to the structural changes arising in bulk metallic glasses (BMGs).
